---- MODULE W4Od1m3p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* Two allocator instances share one runway-clearance record.  A leader is  *)
(* elected among them and only the current-epoch leader may commit a         *)
(* clearance update.  A failed leader steps down and a fresh election bumps   *)
(* the epoch, so a stale instance can never silently overwrite a clearance.   *)

CONSTANT MaxClr

Instances == {"north", "south"}
NoLeader  == "none"

VARIABLES leader, epoch, committed, acked, nextClr

vars == << leader, epoch, committed, acked, nextClr >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Instances \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxClr
    /\ committed \subseteq (1..MaxClr)
    /\ acked \subseteq (1..MaxClr)
    /\ nextClr \in 1..(MaxClr + 1)

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ nextClr = 1

Elect(i) ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ leader' = i
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch < MaxClr THEN epoch + 1 ELSE epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED << committed, acked, nextClr >>

Failover(i) ==
    /\ leader = i
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, committed, acked, nextClr >>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ leader = i
    /\ nextClr <= MaxClr
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {nextClr}
    /\ nextClr' = nextClr + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, epoch, acked >>

Report(c) ==
    /\ c \in committed
    /\ c \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, epoch, committed, nextClr >>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Elect(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Failover(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Commit(i)
    \/ \E c \in 1..MaxClr : Report(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No clearance is ever reported to a tower unless it truly sits in the       *)
(* shared record: every acknowledged update survives in the committed set.    *)
NoLostUpdate == acked \subseteq committed
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANT MaxClr = 4
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator runs as two independent instances, "north" and
"south", that share one runway-clearance record (a single pool of clearance
ids). To keep the shared record consistent the instances run leader election
with failover: at most one instance is the leader at a time, and each election
increments a leadership epoch. Towers submit clearance requests; only the
current leader may commit a clearance into the shared record, and a clearance is
reported back to the requesting tower only after it is durably committed.

The system takes four kinds of steps. Elect(i): when there is no leader, an
instance i becomes leader and the epoch advances. Failover(i): the current
leader i detects it can no longer make progress and steps down, leaving no
leader until the next election. Commit(i): the leader i writes the next clearance
id into the shared committed record. Report(c): a clearance id c that is present
in the committed record is acknowledged back to the tower that requested it.

Because a stepped-down instance loses leadership before a new one is elected,
and because only committed clearances are ever reported, no acknowledged
clearance can be silently dropped or overwritten by a stale instance.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every clearance id that has been reported (acknowledged) back
to a tower is present in the shared committed record, so no acknowledged update
to the shared record is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od3m2p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* An interbank settlement batch runs two-phase commit over three member      *)
(* banks.  Each batch round the coordinator authorizes members; only a member *)
(* authorized in the CURRENT round may vote to prepare, and only a prepared   *)
(* member may apply the settlement.  Authorizations from earlier rounds are    *)
(* stale: a slow member carrying an old authorization must re-authorize before *)
(* it can act again.  Members may be slow but never crash.                     *)

CONSTANT MaxRound

Members == {"boa", "citi", "wells"}

VARIABLES round, authRound, prepared, committed, phase

vars == << round, authRound, prepared, committed, phase >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ authRound \in [Members -> 0..MaxRound]
    /\ prepared \subseteq Members
    /\ committed \subseteq Members
    /\ phase \in {"open", "closed"}

Init ==
    /\ round = 0
    /\ authRound = [m \in Members |-> 0]
    /\ prepared = {}
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ phase = "open"

\* Coordinator grants a current-round authorization to member m.
Authorize(m) ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ authRound' = [authRound EXCEPT ![m] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, prepared, committed, phase >>

\* A member votes to prepare, but only if its authorization is current.
Vote(m) ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ authRound[m] = round
    /\ m \notin prepared
    /\ prepared' = prepared \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, authRound, committed, phase >>

\* A prepared member applies the settlement.
Apply(m) ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ m \in prepared
    /\ m \notin committed
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, authRound, prepared, phase >>

Close ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ phase' = "closed"
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, authRound, prepared, committed >>

\* Open a fresh round; per-round votes reset but stale authorizations persist.
NewRound ==
    /\ phase = "closed"
    /\ round' = IF round < MaxRound THEN round + 1 ELSE round
    /\ prepared' = {}
    /\ committed' = {}
    /\ phase' = "open"
    /\ UNCHANGED authRound

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members : Authorize(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Vote(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Apply(m)
    \/ Close
    \/ NewRound

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No stale or unauthorized member ever applies the settlement: every member  *)
(* that has committed carries an authorization issued in the current round.    *)
NoStaleAction == \A m \in committed : authRound[m] = round
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANT MaxRound = 3
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is applied using two-phase commit across
three member banks ("boa", "citi", "wells"). The batch proceeds in rounds. In
each round the coordinator authorizes members; an authorization is stamped with
the round number in which it was granted. Only a member whose authorization
matches the current round may vote to prepare, and only a prepared member may
apply (commit) the settlement. Members can be slow — they may lag arbitrarily
between authorization, voting, and applying — but they never fail outright.

The system takes these steps. Authorize(m): the coordinator grants member m a
current-round authorization. Vote(m): a member m whose authorization is current
and that has not yet prepared votes to prepare. Apply(m): a prepared member m
applies the settlement into the committed set. Close: the coordinator closes the
current round. NewRound: after a round is closed the coordinator opens the next
round, resetting the per-round prepared and committed sets while the members'
prior authorizations persist and thereby become stale.

Because voting requires a current-round authorization and the committed set is
cleared at every new round, a member carrying only an old (stale) authorization
cannot prepare or apply until it re-authorizes in the new round.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every member that has applied the settlement in the committed
set holds an authorization issued in the current round, so no stale or
unauthorized member ever performs a settlement action.

---- MODULE W4Od6m8p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* An elevator bank in a skyscraper admits passengers into two cars under a    *)
(* hierarchical locking discipline: an agent first takes the coarse bank lock, *)
(* then a fine per-car lock, and only then boards a waiting request into that   *)
(* car.  Boarding requests may be serviced in any order (messages reordered).  *)
(* The whole bank has a fixed occupancy ceiling that boarding must respect.     *)

CONSTANTS BankCap, MaxReq

Agents == {"a1", "a2"}
Cars   == {"c1", "c2"}
Free   == "free"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, load, pending, served

vars == << coarse, fine, load, pending, served >>

TotalLoad == load["c1"] + load["c2"]

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Agents \cup {Free}
    /\ fine \in [Cars -> Agents \cup {Free}]
    /\ load \in [Cars -> Nat]
    /\ pending \subseteq (1..MaxReq)
    /\ served \subseteq (1..MaxReq)

Init ==
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ fine = [c \in Cars |-> Free]
    /\ load = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ pending = 1..MaxReq
    /\ served = {}

AcquireCoarse(a) ==
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ coarse' = a
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, load, pending, served >>

AcquireFine(a, c) ==
    /\ coarse = a
    /\ fine[c] = Free
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![c] = a]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, load, pending, served >>

\* Board any waiting request into a car, respecting the bank ceiling.
Board(a, c, req) ==
    /\ coarse = a
    /\ fine[c] = a
    /\ req \in pending
    /\ TotalLoad < BankCap
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![c] = load[c] + 1]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {req}
    /\ served' = served \cup {req}
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine >>

ReleaseFine(a, c) ==
    /\ fine[c] = a
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![c] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, load, pending, served >>

ReleaseCoarse(a) ==
    /\ coarse = a
    /\ coarse' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, load, pending, served >>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents : AcquireCoarse(a)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, c \in Cars : AcquireFine(a, c)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, c \in Cars, req \in 1..MaxReq : Board(a, c, req)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, c \in Cars : ReleaseFine(a, c)
    \/ \E a \in Agents : ReleaseCoarse(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* The bank never carries more passengers than its fixed occupancy ceiling.    *)
WithinCapacity == TotalLoad <= BankCap
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS BankCap = 4
          MaxReq = 4
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper has two cars ("c1", "c2") and admits waiting
passenger requests into them. Two dispatch agents ("a1", "a2") coordinate using
a hierarchical locking discipline: an agent must first acquire the coarse bank
lock, then acquire the fine lock on a specific car, and only then may it board a
request into that car. Boarding requests may be picked up and serviced in any
order — messages can be reordered — so no fixed request sequence is assumed. The
bank has a fixed total occupancy ceiling that combined boarding across both cars
must never exceed.

The system takes these steps. AcquireCoarse(a): an agent takes the free coarse
bank lock. AcquireFine(a,c): an agent holding the coarse lock takes the free fine
lock on car c. Board(a,c,req): an agent holding both the coarse lock and car c's
fine lock boards a still-waiting request req into car c, but only while the total
number of passengers already carried across both cars is strictly below the bank
ceiling. ReleaseFine(a,c): the holder of car c's fine lock releases it.
ReleaseCoarse(a): the holder of the coarse lock releases it.

Because boarding is guarded by the total-occupancy check and each board adds
exactly one passenger, the combined load can never rise above the ceiling.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of passengers carried across both cars is
always less than or equal to the bank's fixed occupancy ceiling, so the bounded
capacity is never exceeded.

---- MODULE W4Od12m6p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* A blood-bank inventory tracker serialises updates to a shared record with   *)
(* lease-based ownership: a worker must hold an unexpired lease to commit the   *)
(* next update, and leases lapse as the clock advances.  Each committed update  *)
(* is stamped with the next consecutive id, so the durable record forms a       *)
(* gap-free log.  The bank's storage capacity can change at runtime.            *)

CONSTANTS MaxT, TTL, MaxId

Workers == {"w1", "w2"}
NoOne   == "none"

VARIABLES clock, holder, expiry, committed, nextId, capacity

vars == << clock, holder, expiry, committed, nextId, capacity >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT
    /\ holder \in Workers \cup {NoOne}
    /\ expiry \in 0..MaxT
    /\ committed \subseteq (1..MaxId)
    /\ nextId \in 1..(MaxId + 1)
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxId

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ expiry = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ nextId = 1
    /\ capacity = MaxId

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, expiry, committed, nextId, capacity >>

\* Acquire the lease when it is free or has expired; stamp a fresh expiry.
Acquire(w) ==
    /\ (holder = NoOne \/ clock >= expiry)
    /\ holder' = w
    /\ expiry' = IF clock + TTL <= MaxT THEN clock + TTL ELSE MaxT
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, committed, nextId, capacity >>

Release(w) ==
    /\ holder = w
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, expiry, committed, nextId, capacity >>

\* Commit the next consecutive update; requires a still-valid lease and room.
Commit(w) ==
    /\ holder = w
    /\ clock < expiry
    /\ nextId <= MaxId
    /\ Cardinality(committed) < capacity
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {nextId}
    /\ nextId' = nextId + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, holder, expiry, capacity >>

\* Storage capacity is re-provisioned at runtime.
Resize(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, holder, expiry, committed, nextId >>

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Acquire(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Release(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Commit(w)
    \/ \E k \in 1..MaxId : Resize(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No update is ever lost: the durable record is a gap-free prefix of update   *)
(* ids, so if id i is committed then its predecessor i-1 is committed too.      *)
NoLostUpdate == \A i \in committed : (i = 1) \/ ((i - 1) \in committed)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS MaxT = 3
          TTL = 2
          MaxId = 4
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker serialises updates to one shared inventory record
using lease-based ownership with expiry. Two workers ("w1", "w2") contend for a
single lease. A worker may take the lease when it is free or has expired, and the
lease is stamped with an expiry time measured against a global clock that ticks
forward. Only a worker holding a still-valid (unexpired) lease may commit the
next update, and each committed update is stamped with the next consecutive id,
so the durable record is a gap-free log of update ids. The bank's storage
capacity can be re-provisioned at runtime.

The system takes these steps. Tick: the global clock advances by one, which can
cause a held lease to lapse. Acquire(w): a worker takes the lease when it is free
or expired, receiving a fresh expiry. Release(w): the lease holder gives up the
lease. Commit(w): the holder of a valid lease appends the next consecutive update
id to the durable record, provided the record is below its current capacity.
Resize(k): the storage capacity is changed to a new value k at runtime.

Because commits are serialised behind a single valid lease and each stamps the
next consecutive id, the durable record never develops a gap and no update is
skipped or lost.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the durable record is always a gap-free prefix of update ids —
whenever an update id i is committed, its predecessor i-1 is also committed — so
no acknowledged update to the shared record is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od12m5p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* Access to the blood-bank's single critical cold-store is arbitrated by      *)
(* quorum voting: each of three nodes may grant its one vote to at most one     *)
(* requester, and a requester enters the critical section only after gathering  *)
(* a quorum of grants.  Any node may crash silently, losing its vote.  Because  *)
(* votes are exclusive and a quorum is a strict majority, two different nodes    *)
(* can never both assemble a quorum at the same time.                           *)

CONSTANTS Quorum, MaxCrash

Nodes == {"n1", "n2", "n3"}
NoOne == "none"

VARIABLES requesting, grant, cs, crashed

vars == << requesting, grant, cs, crashed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ requesting \subseteq Nodes
    /\ grant \in [Nodes -> Nodes \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ cs \subseteq Nodes
    /\ crashed \subseteq Nodes

Grants(r) == {v \in Nodes : grant[v] = r}

Init ==
    /\ requesting = {}
    /\ grant = [v \in Nodes |-> NoOne]
    /\ cs = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

Request(n) ==
    /\ n \notin requesting
    /\ n \notin cs
    /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED << grant, cs, crashed >>

\* A live voter with a free vote grants it to a requester.
Grant(v, r) ==
    /\ v \notin crashed
    /\ grant[v] = NoOne
    /\ r \in requesting
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![v] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED << requesting, cs, crashed >>

\* A voter reclaims its vote from a requester that has not yet entered.
Yield(v) ==
    /\ grant[v] # NoOne
    /\ grant[v] \notin cs
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![v] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED << requesting, cs, crashed >>

\* Enter the critical section once a quorum has been gathered.
Enter(r) ==
    /\ r \in requesting
    /\ cs = {}
    /\ Cardinality(Grants(r)) >= Quorum
    /\ cs' = {r}
    /\ requesting' = requesting \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << grant, crashed >>

Exit(r) ==
    /\ r \in cs
    /\ cs' = {}
    /\ grant' = [v \in Nodes |-> IF grant[v] = r THEN NoOne ELSE grant[v]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << requesting, crashed >>

\* A node crashes silently, dropping the vote it may have granted.
Crash(v) ==
    /\ v \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) < MaxCrash
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {v}
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![v] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED << requesting, cs >>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Request(n)
    \/ \E v \in Nodes, r \in Nodes : Grant(v, r)
    \/ \E v \in Nodes : Yield(v)
    \/ \E r \in Nodes : Enter(r)
    \/ \E r \in Nodes : Exit(r)
    \/ \E v \in Nodes : Crash(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Two distinct nodes can never both hold a quorum of grants simultaneously,   *)
(* which is what guarantees mutually exclusive access to the cold-store.        *)
QuorumExclusion ==
    \A a, b \in Nodes :
        (Cardinality(Grants(a)) >= Quorum /\ Cardinality(Grants(b)) >= Quorum)
            => a = b
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS Quorum = 2
          MaxCrash = 1
INVARIANT QuorumExclusion
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards access to its single critical cold-store
using quorum voting on each action. Three nodes ("n1", "n2", "n3") each hold one
vote. A node that wants the cold-store requests it; other nodes may each grant
their single vote to one requester, and a requester enters the critical section
only after it has gathered a quorum (a strict majority) of grants. At most one
participant may crash silently, which drops the vote it had granted. Votes are
exclusive: a voter that has granted its vote cannot grant it again until it
reclaims or crashes.

The system takes these steps. Request(n): a node not already requesting and not
in the critical section asks for the cold-store. Grant(v,r): a live voter v with
a free vote grants it to a requester r. Yield(v): a voter reclaims its vote from
a requester that has not yet entered the critical section. Enter(r): a requester
that has gathered a quorum of grants, and while no one else is in the critical
section, enters it and stops requesting. Exit(r): the occupant leaves the
critical section and all votes granted to it are released. Crash(v): a node
crashes silently (at most one such crash occurs) and the vote it had granted is
dropped.

Because each voter's vote is exclusive and a quorum is a strict majority, two
different nodes can never simultaneously hold a quorum of grants.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no two distinct nodes ever simultaneously hold a quorum of
grants, so the critical cold-store is accessed by at most one node at a time —
mutual exclusion of the critical resource holds.

---- MODULE W4Od16m6p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

(* A pharmacy prescription dispenser allocates fill slots under lease-based    *)
(* ownership with expiry.  To allocate a slot a dispenser must hold that slot's *)
(* unexpired lease, and a slot's lease is exclusive.  Once a slot is allocated  *)
(* its lease is frozen to the allocating dispenser, so a second (or slow, stale)*)
(* dispenser can never re-lease and double-allocate the same slot.  Dispensers  *)
(* may be slow but never fail.  When every slot is filled a new batch resets.   *)

CONSTANTS MaxT, TTL

Slots      == {"s1", "s2"}
Dispensers == {"d1", "d2"}
NoOne      == "none"

VARIABLES clock, leaseHolder, leaseExp, allocTo

vars == << clock, leaseHolder, leaseExp, allocTo >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT
    /\ leaseHolder \in [Slots -> Dispensers \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ leaseExp \in [Slots -> 0..MaxT]
    /\ allocTo \in [Slots -> Dispensers \cup {NoOne}]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ leaseHolder = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
    /\ leaseExp = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ allocTo = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << leaseHolder, leaseExp, allocTo >>

\* Take an unallocated slot's lease when it is free or expired.
Acquire(d, s) ==
    /\ allocTo[s] = NoOne
    /\ (leaseHolder[s] = NoOne \/ clock >= leaseExp[s])
    /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![s] = d]
    /\ leaseExp' = [leaseExp EXCEPT ![s] = IF clock + TTL <= MaxT THEN clock + TTL ELSE MaxT]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, allocTo >>

ReleaseLease(d, s) ==
    /\ leaseHolder[s] = d
    /\ allocTo[s] = NoOne
    /\ leaseHolder' = [leaseHolder EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, leaseExp, allocTo >>

\* Allocate the slot; only the holder of a still-valid lease may do so.
Allocate(d, s) ==
    /\ leaseHolder[s] = d
    /\ clock < leaseExp[s]
    /\ allocTo[s] = NoOne
    /\ allocTo' = [allocTo EXCEPT ![s] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, leaseHolder, leaseExp >>

\* Start a fresh prescription batch once every slot is filled.
Reset ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots : allocTo[s] # NoOne
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ leaseHolder' = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
    /\ leaseExp' = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ allocTo' = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers, s \in Slots : Acquire(d, s)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers, s \in Slots : ReleaseLease(d, s)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers, s \in Slots : Allocate(d, s)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Every allocated slot is allocated to precisely the dispenser that holds its *)
(* lease; since the lease is exclusive and frozen after allocation, no slot is  *)
(* ever double-allocated to a second dispenser.                                 *)
AllocMatchesLease ==
    \A s \in Slots : allocTo[s] # NoOne => allocTo[s] = leaseHolder[s]
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS MaxT = 3
          TTL = 2
INVARIANT AllocMatchesLease
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser allocates fill slots ("s1", "s2") to two
dispensing units ("d1", "d2") using lease-based ownership with expiry. To
allocate a slot a unit must first hold that slot's lease, and each slot's lease
is exclusive to a single holder. Leases carry an expiry measured against a global
clock that ticks forward, and a unit may take a slot's lease only while the slot
is unallocated and its lease is free or has expired. Once a slot is allocated,
its lease is frozen to the allocating unit and cannot be re-leased. Dispensing
units may be slow — lagging arbitrarily between acquiring a lease and allocating
— but they never fail.

The system takes these steps. Tick: the global clock advances by one, possibly
expiring a lease. Acquire(d,s): a unit takes the lease on an unallocated slot
whose lease is free or expired, receiving a fresh expiry. ReleaseLease(d,s): a
unit releases the lease on a slot it has not yet allocated. Allocate(d,s): the
holder of a slot's still-valid lease allocates that slot to itself, provided the
slot is not already allocated. Reset: once every slot is allocated, a new
prescription batch clears all slots and leases and restarts the clock.

Because allocation requires an exclusive, unexpired lease and the lease is frozen
to the allocating unit afterward, no slot can be re-leased and handed to a second
unit — the same slot is never allocated twice.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every allocated slot is allocated to exactly the dispensing unit
that holds its lease, so no slot is ever double-allocated to two different units.

---- MODULE W4Od14m0p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* A wildfire drone surveillance swarm deploys retardant on targets.  A        *)
(* retardant drop is irreversible and must happen at most once per target.     *)
(* Drones use optimistic locking with retry: a drone snapshots a target's       *)
(* version, and its drop commits only if the version is still unchanged, which  *)
(* also bumps the version so any concurrent stale attempt must abort and retry. *)
(* One drone may crash silently, abandoning its in-flight attempt.              *)

CONSTANTS MaxV, MaxCrash

Targets == {"t1", "t2"}
Drones  == {"dr1", "dr2"}
NoTgt   == "none"

VARIABLES ver, drops, snapTgt, snapVer, crashed

vars == << ver, drops, snapTgt, snapVer, crashed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in [Targets -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ drops \in [Targets -> Nat]
    /\ snapTgt \in [Drones -> Targets \cup {NoTgt}]
    /\ snapVer \in [Drones -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Drones

Init ==
    /\ ver = [t \in Targets |-> 0]
    /\ drops = [t \in Targets |-> 0]
    /\ snapTgt = [d \in Drones |-> NoTgt]
    /\ snapVer = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}

\* Snapshot a not-yet-hit target's current version to attempt a drop.
Prepare(d, t) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ snapTgt[d] = NoTgt
    /\ drops[t] = 0
    /\ snapTgt' = [snapTgt EXCEPT ![d] = t]
    /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![d] = ver[t]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << ver, drops, crashed >>

(* swap registers.  A worker allocates a requested slot only by a successful     *)
(* CAS from the empty owner to itself; a CAS against an already-owned slot fails *)
(* and the request is retried elsewhere.  The spool's capacity changes at        *)
(* runtime.  Because each allocation is one successful CAS on a distinct empty    *)
(* slot, the count of allocation events equals the number of owned slots.        *)

CONSTANT MaxCap

Slots   == {"j1", "j2", "j3"}
Workers == {"wk1", "wk2"}
Empty   == "empty"

VARIABLES owner, allocCount, capacity, queue

vars == << owner, allocCount, capacity, queue >>

Owned == {s \in Slots : owner[s] # Empty}

    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Workers \cup {Empty}]
    /\ allocCount \in Nat
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap
    /\ queue \subseteq Slots

    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Empty]
    /\ allocCount = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ queue = {}

    /\ s \notin queue
    /\ owner[s] = Empty
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, allocCount, capacity >>

CAS(w, s) ==
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ owner[s] = Empty
    /\ Cardinality(Owned) < capacity
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = w]
    /\ allocCount' = allocCount + 1
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Retry(s) ==
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ owner[s] # Empty
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, allocCount, capacity >>

Resize(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, allocCount, queue >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Request(s)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, s \in Slots : CAS(w, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Retry(s)
    \/ \E k \in 1..MaxCap : Resize(k)

(* equals the number of distinct owned slots, so each owned slot was claimed by  *)
(* exactly one CAS.                                                              *)

    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = w]

    /\ owner[j] = w

    /\ doneCount' = 0

    \/ \E i \in Instances : AcquireFine(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Enter(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Exit(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Any instance in the critical section holds the exclusive fine print-head      *)
(* lock; since the fine lock has a single holder, at most one instance uses the   *)
(* print head at a time -- mutual exclusion of the critical resource.             *)
MutualExclusion == \A i \in cs : fine = i
====

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A print shop job spooler guards its single print head — the critical resource —
using hierarchical locks (coarse then fine). Two spooler instances ("i1", "i2")
contend for the print head. An instance must first hold the coarse spooler lock,
then acquire the fine print-head lock, and only while holding both may it enter
the critical section to use the print head. Instances may be slow — they request
the resource and can lag arbitrarily — but they never fail.

The system takes these steps. Request(i): a (possibly slow) instance not already
in the critical section asks for the print head. AcquireCoarse(i): an instance
takes the free coarse spooler lock. AcquireFine(i): an instance holding the
coarse lock takes the free fine print-head lock. Enter(i): an instance that has
requested the head and holds both locks enters the critical section, but only
while the critical section is empty. Exit(i): the occupant leaves the critical
section and releases both the fine and coarse locks.

Because entering requires the exclusive fine print-head lock and that lock has a
single holder, no two instances can be in the critical section at the same time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every instance in the critical section holds the exclusive fine
print-head lock, so at most one instance ever uses the print head at a time —
mutual exclusion of the critical resource holds.

---- MODULE W4Od18m9p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* A smart-home door lock network elects a single master hub -- the critical     *)
(* resource -- among nodes provisioned in the current epoch.  Epoch-numbered      *)
(* reconfiguration revokes mastership: a new epoch clears the master so a node    *)
(* must be provisioned in the current epoch to be granted it.  The provisioning   *)
(* capacity changes at runtime.  At most one node ever holds the master role.     *)

CONSTANTS MaxEpoch, MaxNodes

Nodes == {"n1", "n2", "n3"}

VARIABLES epoch, holders, provEpoch, capacity

vars == << epoch, holders, provEpoch, capacity >>

ProvisionedNow == {n \in Nodes : provEpoch[n] = epoch}

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ holders \subseteq Nodes
    /\ provEpoch \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxNodes

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ holders = {}
    /\ provEpoch = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ capacity = MaxNodes

\* Reconfiguration advances the epoch and revokes the master role.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ holders' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED << provEpoch, capacity >>

\* Provision a node in the current epoch, bounded by the current capacity.
Provision(n) ==
    /\ provEpoch[n] # epoch
    /\ Cardinality(ProvisionedNow) < capacity
    /\ provEpoch' = [provEpoch EXCEPT ![n] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, holders, capacity >>

\* Grant the master role, but only when it is currently unheld.
Grant(n) ==
    /\ holders = {}
    /\ provEpoch[n] = epoch
    /\ holders' = holders \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, provEpoch, capacity >>

Yield(n) ==
    /\ n \in holders
    /\ holders' = holders \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, provEpoch, capacity >>

Resize(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, holders, provEpoch >>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Provision(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Grant(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Yield(n)
    \/ \E k \in 1..MaxNodes : Resize(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* At most one node ever holds the master hub role -- mutual exclusion of the    *)
(* critical resource.                                                            *)
MutualExclusion == \A a, b \in holders : a = b
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS MaxEpoch = 2
          MaxNodes = 3
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A smart-home door lock network elects a single master hub — the critical resource
— among its nodes ("n1", "n2", "n3"). The network runs epoch-numbered
reconfiguration: mastership is granted only to a node provisioned in the current
epoch, and advancing to a new epoch revokes the current master and stales all
prior provisioning. The provisioning capacity — the number of nodes that may be
provisioned in an epoch — changes at runtime. At most one node ever holds the
master role.

The system takes these steps. Reconfigure: the network advances the epoch and
clears the current master. Provision(n): a node is provisioned in the current
epoch, provided the number of nodes already provisioned this epoch is below the
current capacity. Grant(n): a node provisioned in the current epoch is granted
the master role, but only while the role is currently unheld. Yield(n): the
current master relinquishes the role. Resize(k): the provisioning capacity is
changed to a new value k at runtime.

Because the master role is granted only while it is unheld and every
reconfiguration clears it, no two nodes can ever simultaneously hold mastership.

SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one node ever holds the master hub role at a time, so
mutual exclusion of the critical resource holds.

---- MODULE W4Od16m3p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

(* A pharmacy prescription dispenser runs as two instances that share one pool   *)
(* of prescriptions and coordinate by leader election with failover.  Only the   *)
(* current leader may dispense, and dispensing a prescription is an irreversible  *)
(* action that must happen at most once.  Each dispense is appended to an audit   *)
(* log that must never name the same prescription twice.                         *)

CONSTANT MaxEpoch

Instances == {"phA", "phB"}
Scripts   == {"rx1", "rx2"}
NoLeader  == "none"

VARIABLES leader, epoch, dispenseLog, pool

vars == << leader, epoch, dispenseLog, pool >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Instances \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ dispenseLog \in Seq(Scripts)
    /\ pool \subseteq Scripts

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ dispenseLog = << >>
    /\ pool = Scripts

Elect(i) ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ leader' = i
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch < MaxEpoch THEN epoch + 1 ELSE epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED << dispenseLog, pool >>

Failover(i) ==
    /\ leader = i
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, dispenseLog, pool >>

\* Only the leader dispenses; a script leaves the pool so it is never redone.
Dispense(i, rx) ==
    /\ leader = i
    /\ rx \in pool
    /\ dispenseLog' = Append(dispenseLog, rx)
    /\ pool' = pool \ {rx}
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, epoch >>

Reset ==
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ epoch' = 0
    /\ dispenseLog' = << >>
    /\ pool' = Scripts

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Elect(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Failover(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, rx \in Scripts : Dispense(i, rx)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* The irreversible dispense happens at most once per prescription: no script    *)
(* is ever named twice in the audit log.                                         *)
DispenseAtMostOnce ==
    \A a, b \in 1..Len(dispenseLog) : (dispenseLog[a] = dispenseLog[b]) => (a = b)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANT MaxEpoch = 3
INVARIANT DispenseAtMostOnce
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser runs as two instances ("phA", "phB") that share
one pool of prescriptions ("rx1", "rx2") and coordinate by leader election with
failover. At most one instance is the leader at a time; a failed leader steps
down and a fresh election bumps a leadership epoch. Only the current leader may
dispense a prescription, and dispensing is an irreversible action that must
happen at most once per prescription. Every dispense is appended to an audit log
that must never name the same prescription twice.

The system takes these steps. Elect(i): when there is no leader, an instance
becomes leader and the epoch advances. Failover(i): the current leader steps
down, leaving no leader until the next election. Dispense(i,rx): the leader
dispenses a prescription still in the shared pool, appending it to the audit log
and removing it from the pool so it cannot be dispensed again. Reset: once the
pool is empty, a new batch restores the pool and clears the log.

Because a prescription leaves the shared pool the moment it is dispensed and only
in-pool prescriptions can be dispensed, no prescription is ever dispensed or
logged a second time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no prescription is ever named more than once in the dispensing
audit log, so the irreversible dispense action happens at most once per
prescription.

---- MODULE W4Od12m9p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

(* A blood-bank inventory tracker moves a fixed supply of blood units between a  *)
(* central store and a fridge.  Epoch-numbered reconfiguration re-routes the      *)
(* network without touching the units.  Transfer requests are serviced in any     *)
(* order (messages reordered): a shipped unit leaves its location into transit    *)
(* and is later delivered to a destination.  The total supply is conserved.       *)

CONSTANTS MaxEpoch, MaxReq, Total

Locations == {"central", "fridge"}

VARIABLES epoch, stock, inTransit, pending

vars == << epoch, stock, inTransit, pending >>

OnHand == stock["central"] + stock["fridge"]

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ stock \in [Locations -> 0..Total]
    /\ inTransit \in 0..Total
    /\ pending \subseteq (1..MaxReq)

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ stock = [l \in Locations |-> IF l = "central" THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ inTransit = 0
    /\ pending = 1..MaxReq

\* Reconfigure the routing epoch; units are untouched.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << stock, inTransit, pending >>

\* Ship a unit out of a location into transit, servicing any pending request.
Ship(l, req) ==
    /\ stock[l] > 0
    /\ req \in pending
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit + 1
    /\ pending' = pending \ {req}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* Deliver an in-transit unit to a destination location.
Deliver(l) ==
    /\ inTransit > 0
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit - 1
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, pending >>

\* Once all requests are serviced and transit is clear, open a new batch.
Reset ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ inTransit = 0
    /\ epoch' = 0
    /\ stock' = [l \in Locations |-> IF l = "central" THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ inTransit' = 0
    /\ pending' = 1..MaxReq

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E l \in Locations, req \in 1..MaxReq : Ship(l, req)
    \/ \E l \in Locations : Deliver(l)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* Blood units are conserved: on-hand stock plus units in transit always equals  *)
(* the fixed total supply -- nothing is created or destroyed.                    *)
Conservation == OnHand + inTransit = Total
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS MaxEpoch = 2
          MaxReq = 4
          Total = 3
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker moves a fixed supply of blood units between a
central store and a fridge. The network runs epoch-numbered reconfiguration that
re-routes transfers without ever creating or destroying units. Transfer requests
are serviced in any order — messages can be reordered: a shipped unit leaves its
source location into transit and is later delivered to a destination. The total
supply of blood units is conserved.

The system takes these steps. Reconfigure: the routing epoch advances, leaving
all unit counts untouched. Ship(l,req): a unit leaves location l into transit,
servicing any pending transfer request chosen in arbitrary order. Deliver(l): an
in-transit unit is delivered into location l. Reset: once all requests are
serviced and nothing is in transit, a fresh batch restores the initial
distribution.

Because every ship moves exactly one unit from a location into transit and every
delivery moves exactly one unit from transit into a location, and reconfiguration
touches no counts, the total number of units never changes.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the on-hand stock across all locations plus the units in transit
always equals the fixed total supply, so no blood unit is ever created or
destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od1m1p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* An air-traffic runway allocator grants exclusive slot access with a token     *)
(* ring: the token circulates among controllers and only the token holder may    *)
(* allocate a requested runway slot.  A privileged admin override may allocate a  *)
(* slot without the token.  A slot is claimed only while unowned, so the count of *)
(* allocation events equals the number of owned slots -- no slot is allocated     *)
(* twice.                                                                         *)

Ctrls == {"a1", "a2", "a3"}
Slots == {"s1", "s2", "s3"}
None  == "none"
Admin == "admin"

RingNext(n) == CASE n = "a1" -> "a2"
                 [] n = "a2" -> "a3"
                 [] n = "a3" -> "a1"

VARIABLES token, owner, allocCount, queue

vars == << token, owner, allocCount, queue >>

Owned == {s \in Slots : owner[s] # None}

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Ctrls
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Ctrls \cup {Admin, None}]
    /\ allocCount \in 0..Cardinality(Slots)
    /\ queue \subseteq Slots

Init ==
    /\ token = "a1"
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> None]
    /\ allocCount = 0
    /\ queue = {}

\* The token advances around the ring.
PassToken(i) ==
    /\ token = i
    /\ token' = RingNext(i)
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, allocCount, queue >>

Request(s) ==
    /\ s \notin queue
    /\ owner[s] = None
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, owner, allocCount >>

\* Only the token holder allocates, and only an unowned requested slot.
Allocate(i, s) ==
    /\ token = i
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ owner[s] = None
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = i]
    /\ allocCount' = allocCount + 1
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED token

\* Privileged admin override: allocate an unowned slot without the token.
AdminAllocate(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] = None
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Admin]
    /\ allocCount' = allocCount + 1
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Ctrls : PassToken(i)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Request(s)
    \/ \E i \in Ctrls, s \in Slots : Allocate(i, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminAllocate(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No slot is ever allocated twice: the number of allocation events equals the   *)
(* number of distinct owned slots.                                               *)
NoDoubleAllocation == allocCount = Cardinality(Owned)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator grants exclusive slot access using a token ring.
The token circulates among three controllers ("a1", "a2", "a3"), and only the
controller currently holding the token may allocate a requested runway slot
("s1", "s2", "s3"). There is a privileged admin override: an administrator may
allocate a slot directly without holding the token. A slot may be claimed only
while it is unowned, so the same slot is never allocated twice.

The system takes these steps. PassToken(i): the token holder passes the token to
the next controller around the ring. Request(s): an unowned, not-yet-requested
slot is placed on the request queue. Allocate(i,s): the token holder allocates a
requested, still-unowned slot to itself, recording one allocation event.
AdminAllocate(s): the privileged admin override allocates an unowned slot without
the token, recording one allocation event.

Because a slot can be claimed only while unowned and each allocation event —
whether by the token holder or the admin — fills a distinct unowned slot, the
running count of allocation events stays equal to the number of owned slots.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of allocation events always equals the number of
distinct owned slots, so no runway slot is ever double-allocated.

---- MODULE W4Od13m7p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

(* A vending machine network commits inventory updates to one shared version     *)
(* register that two instances share.  Updates use a compare-and-swap: an         *)
(* instance advances the register by one and records the new version as           *)
(* committed; a contended CAS may fail and must be retried.  Because each          *)
(* successful CAS records exactly the version it installed, the committed set is   *)
(* the full prefix of versions and no update is ever lost.                        *)

CONSTANT MaxVer

Instances == {"v1", "v2"}

VARIABLES reg, committed, acked, casFails

vars == << reg, committed, acked, casFails >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ committed \subseteq (1..MaxVer)
    /\ acked \subseteq (1..MaxVer)
    /\ casFails \in 0..MaxVer

Init ==
    /\ reg = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ casFails = 0

\* Successful CAS: advance the register and record the installed version.
CASUpdate(i) ==
    /\ reg < MaxVer
    /\ reg' = reg + 1
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {reg + 1}
    /\ UNCHANGED << acked, casFails >>

\* A contended CAS fails and is retried (bounded book-keeping).
AbortCAS(i) ==
    /\ casFails < MaxVer
    /\ casFails' = casFails + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, committed, acked >>

\* Acknowledge a committed version back to a client.
Ack(v) ==
    /\ v \in committed
    /\ v \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, committed, casFails >>

\* Once the register is full, a fresh inventory cycle resets it.
Reset ==
    /\ reg = MaxVer
    /\ reg' = 0
    /\ committed' = {}
    /\ acked' = {}
    /\ casFails' = 0

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CASUpdate(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : AbortCAS(i)
    \/ \E v \in 1..MaxVer : Ack(v)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* No update is lost: the committed set contains the entire prefix of versions   *)
(* up to the current register value, with no gaps.                              *)
NoLostUpdate == \A v \in 1..reg : v \in committed
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANT MaxVer = 4
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A vending machine network commits inventory updates to one shared version
register that two instances ("v1", "v2") share. Updates use a compare-and-swap:
an instance advances the register by one and records the newly installed version
as committed. Because a CAS is atomic, two contending instances never clobber
each other's update — a contended CAS simply fails and is retried. A committed
version may be acknowledged back to a client. Since each successful CAS records
exactly the version it installed, the committed set forms the full prefix of
versions and no update is ever lost.

The system takes these steps. CASUpdate(i): an instance performs a successful
compare-and-swap, advancing the register by one and recording the new version as
committed. AbortCAS(i): a contended compare-and-swap fails and is retried,
advancing only bounded retry book-keeping. Ack(v): a committed version is
acknowledged to a client. Reset: once the register reaches its maximum, a fresh
inventory cycle clears the register and the committed and acknowledged sets.

Because every successful CAS records the exact version it installs and versions
advance by one, the committed set always contains every version from one up to
the current register value, with no gaps.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the committed set always contains the entire prefix of versions
up to the current register value, so no update to the shared register is ever
lost.
